note_tweet.text:
The rulebook of American professional golf contained the phrase "Caucasian race only" until 1961.

Charlie Sifford spent years trying to get it removed.
When he finally played, people kicked his ball into the rough and put human waste in the cup before he reached the green.

He had learned the game as a caddie in Charlotte, and he was good enough to win the Negro National Open six times while being barred from the tour that mattered.

The PGA's constitution restricted membership to golfers of the Caucasian race. Sifford, with the help of the California attorney general, forced its removal in 1961.

He was forty when he finally got a card.

He played with galleries shouting at him, with threats phoned to his hotel, with his ball moved, and with tournaments in the South simply declining to invite him — which was legal, because invitations were discretionary.

He won twice on tour. He was never once invited to the Masters, which used its own invitation rules to keep him out through his entire prime.

He carried a cigar everywhere and refused to stop smoking it on the course, which annoyed people, which was rather the point.

Tiger Woods called him the grandpa he never had and said he would not have had a career without him.

In 2014 he was given the Presidential Medal of Freedom. He died the following year at ninety-two.

He got a sentence deleted from a rulebook. That was the whole fight, and it took him most of his best years.

note_tweet.text:
NFL Legend & Hall of Famer Jerome Bettis reveals he paid $250,000 for a SUPER BOWL SUITE and effectively played the entire PLAYOFFS for free

Jerome Bettis: "I'm trying to get a suite for the Super Bowl for my parents. I had a box in Pittsburgh, so I'm like that would be the perfect thing to have a box in Detroit for the family."

Jerome Bettis: "I ended up with 70 tickets that I paid for the Super Bowl. Everything go off without a hitch. Beautiful. Won the Super Bowl. I get the bill. I couldn't believe... I played the game for free!"

Matt Barnes: "What'd they hit you for?"

Jerome Bettis: "$250,000! For the box! I played the whole playoffs for free! But you know what? You can't get that moment back. I lost my father that Thanksgiving, so he got a chance to see it, in his element where he was holding court. It was worth every penny."
